previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and prior stents, was admitted for exertional chest pain, shortness of breath, orthopnea, and leg swelling. Initial evaluation ruled out acute myocardial infarction with normal EKGs and negative cardiac enzymes. He was found to have acute diastolic heart failure, treated with IV furosemide and transitioned to an increased oral dose of 60 mg daily. Cardiac catheterization revealed significant stent restenosis in the OM1, OM2, and circumflex arteries, which were successfully treated with cutting and kissing balloon angioplasty. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged home in stable condition on his prior medications with the addition of vitamin D for cardiovascular risk reduction. Follow-up was arranged with cardiology to discuss potential surgical options given the extent of disease.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery

for trigger of decompensated heart failure. Fluid status was 
monitored by strict ins/outs and daily weights.  Patient was

congestion normalized.  Patient was given prescription to have 
electrolytes checked in one week, as he had been started on

cardiopulmonary assessment to allow more optimal management of 
congestive heart failure at home.

negative cycled cardiac enzymes.   Continued aspirin, plavix, 
b-blocker and statin for secondary prevention of vascular 
events.  If anginal symptoms persist despite optimization of 
congestive heart failure, could consider the  addition of a long 
acting nitrate to maximize medical therapy.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted with intermittent shortness of breath, weight 
gain and lower extremity swelling: all signs that you had an 
exacerbation of your heart failure.  Your EKG was not 
significantly different and your cardiac enzymes were negative, 
indicating that you did not have a heart attack.  We treated you 
with a diuretic called lasix to help remove the extra fluid from 
your body.  We also started you on a new medication called 
spironolactone.  Your symptoms improved and by the time of 
discharge you were breathing comfortably on room air.   
To keep your heart disease stable, you need to adhere to a low 
salt diet.  You should also try to limit your fluid intake to 
approximately 1.5L/ day (about 3 bottles of water).  You should 
also weight yourself every day and if your weight increases ___ 
lbs, call your cardiologist as this may be an early sign that 
fluid is accumulating.  

Please take all of your medications as previously prescribed:  
In addition, you should take spironolactone 25mg daily.

going to your primary care appointment on ___.

should be on Actos, one of your diabetes medications, longterm.

lightheadness, leg swelling or any other concerning symptoms 
please call your physician or return to the emergency 
department.
